content.thinking:
This piece explains peer review as a process-transparency intervention, touching on competence, integrity, and accountability through self-correction and consensus across independent experts. I'd estimate this raises trust moderately, maybe +2.0 to +2.5, since it's a well-crafted, on-target explanation of scientific quality control.

With anchoring, other measures shift only modestly: trust_post around +1.4, distrust_post around -1.2, and smaller boosts to funding perceptions, institutional trust, policy engagement, and belief/concern items (all roughly +0.3 to +0.9), with negligible effects on donation and newsletter signup. There's a small chance the mention of rejection/gatekeeping could read as suppressing dissent to skeptical audiences, slightly muting the effect, so I'll settle trust around +2.1.

parsed_output.reasoning_summary: This arm is a process-transparency message: it explains peer review as adversarial quality control by competing experts, emphasizing accountability, rejection of weak work, and required revisions. Mechanistically it targets the competence, integrity and openness facets of the multidimensional trust battery quite directly, and it closes with an implicit consensus cue ('experts from across the world consistently reach the same conclusions'), so I expect an above-median but not top-tier primary effect (~+2.1 points, d≈0.09), slightly muted because the text is didactic rather than narrative/messenger-based and because mentioning that many studies are 'rejected and not published' can cue gatekeeping suspicion among skeptics. trust_post and belief_post are re-asked items with pre-treatment anchors, so I shrink them to roughly 60–40% of the fresh-battery effect; distrust falls a bit less in absolute magnitude than trust rises (asymmetric, floor-ish for many respondents). Downstream constructs the text never addresses (federal research funding levels, scientists' policy advocacy role, concern, policy support, behavior) get sub-point effects that fade with distance from the credibility mechanism; inst_trust_mean is further diluted by the federal-government item. Incentivized outcomes get near-zero but slightly positive values consistent with a few cents on the $10 donation and well under two percentage points on real newsletter sign-up.
